content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Coroutine Scopes and Contexts** as part of **Coroutines, Asynchronous Programming, and Concurrency**. String operations return values that should be handled explicitly; choose templates for interpolation and regular expressions only when pattern matching is the right abstraction. Use the subtopics—CoroutineScope, Coroutine Context and Jobs, Dispatchers and Execution Context—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous code introduces lifecycle, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Structured concurrency and explicit data flow make these concerns easier to reason about.

items.title: CoroutineScope
items.text: CoroutineScope depends on task lifetime and execution context. Keep child tasks inside an owning scope, handle cancellation cooperatively, and avoid unsynchronized shared mutable state.

content_blocks.text: A suspend function always runs on a background thread automatically.
